name: Bitcall
description: Telecom services: non-VoIP numbers for SMS/OTP verification, travel eSIM data plans, worldwide VoIP calling, and HLR/MNP number lookup. Email-only signup, no KYC. Paid from a prepaid account balance topped up with Bitcoin, USDT (TRC-20, ERC-20), Ethereum, Monero or card. Once funded, OTP activations, eSIM orders and HLR lookups can be placed through a REST API; VoIP calling is not in the API.

agent_endpoints.auth_note: Two headers on every request: x-key-id and x-api-secret. Keys are created in the Bitcall web panel; the secret is shown once. Endpoints under /v1/otp, /v1/esim and /v1/hlr spend from one prepaid account balance (GET /v1/balance, EUR). The API cannot fund that balance: a purchase without funds returns 409 INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE, and top-up happens at the web checkout. API is in beta and polling-based (no webhooks).

source_attribution: Submitted by Bitcall and relayed by Boyd on 2026-10-02. Checked against the merchant's own pages at 2026-10-02T18:36:50Z. bitcall.io lists top-up by Bitcoin, USDT (TRC-20, ERC-20), Ethereum and Monero (XMR); docs.bitcall.io documents the gateway at https://api.bitcall.io (OTP, eSIM, HLR), says outright that the eSIM API has no top-up operation, and returns INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE with 'Top up, then send the purchase again'. agent_callable_tier is therefore human-checkout, not full-api: an agent can order but cannot pay unaided, the same reasoning as the namecheap correction of 2026-09-16. Differences from the submission: it says 199 eSIM destinations, while bitcall.io/esim says '195+', so no count is written here. bitcall.io/esim also lists USDC and SOL, which the submission and the homepage top-up list do not, and no chain is named for USDC, so neither is recorded as a rail and accepts_usdc stays false. Ethereum and Monero settle but have no rail value in the schema; they appear in the description only. No payment was made, so every rail health is unknown.
